_comment: Channel topology for the CCV core, from the block-level grill-me
(2026-09-23). Every channel is one port on each of two blocks, so this
list IS the design's connectivity and the per-block port index is a
lookup into it rather than a second source.
WHAT IS HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. The topology -- which blocks, which
direction, what rate, what fields -- is complete and checked. Field
WIDTHS are not: most firm up in the per-block session that owns the
interface, and inventing them here would put a number in the generated
typedef that nobody decided. So payload structs are generated only for
channels whose widths are settled; the rest generate topology alone.
COMMON PORTS are not channels and are not listed here -- see
common_ports below. Every block declares them, generated rather than
COUNTS. 40 channels. The source spec's prose says 32 and its per-block
port index runs low on 7 of 14 blocks; the enumerated tables are
self-consistent and are what this file follows. tools/gen-interfaces.py
derives the per-block counts from the channel list so the two can never

common_ports.name: core_clk
common_ports.doc: The core clock, UNGATED -- the only clock a block receives. The block gates it as its first act, inside the block, on its own quiescence or stall; the gated `<blk>_core_clk` never leaves the block, and nothing but the gate and the wake detector may be clocked on this one (CCV-L22). Gating is inside the block, not at the top, so the top holds nothing but block instances and nets (rtl-coding-style.md, "The top level") and the signals that decide sleep stay internal.

common_ports.name: rst_n
common_ports.doc: Synchronous reset, ACTIVE LOW. `CCV_RST is the in-reset condition, so a block spells it `!rst_n`.

common_ports.name: kill_valid
common_ports.doc: Grid teardown, one cycle ahead of the mask, broadcast by RAU to the eight blocks that own warp state (FET, DEC, OOE, RCU, MIU, SPM, SYU, PCA). Lanes hold no warp-tagged state that survives RCU ceasing to send, and DCU, MLC and EXB are physically addressed with no notion of a warp, so they take no part. Outside the credit scheme: a kill must not wait on a stalled receiver.

common_ports.name: kill_warp_mask
common_ports.doc: Warps to discard, one bit per warp CONTEXT (CCV_WARP_CONTEXTS = 32: tier-1 and parked), driven by RAU. It was sized to the four tier-1 warps, but PCA and SYU hold state for parked warps, which a tier-1 mask cannot name. Grid ID appears on no interface -- RAU converts it from its warp-to-CTA-to-grid tables.

common_ports.name: kill_epoch
common_ports.doc: Epoch of the kill being broadcast. Every ack echoes it, so a late ack from a previous kill cannot satisfy this one.

common_ports.name: kill_ack
common_ports.doc: QUIESCED, not merely stopped: a block acks only when it holds no state for the killed warps AND has nothing in flight toward anyone else on their behalf. MIU is the awkward one: retired stores must still drain, so its ack waits on them, while its pending loads are dropped. Gathered at RAU as kill_acks, one bit per owning block in the order FET, DEC, OOE, RCU, MIU, SPM, SYU, PCA. OOE's ack also waits until the epoch notice it sent for the kill (epoch_only on ccv_ooe_fet_redirect, A-74) has landed in FET: its send cycle plus the channel's fixed latency. RAU relaunches only after every ack, so a relaunch can never reach FET ahead of the notice, and no relaunched warp is fetched under an epoch older than OOE's (V-57). A demotion follows the same rule on ccv_ooe_rau_drained.

common_ports.name: kill_ack_epoch
common_ports.doc: The kill_epoch this ack answers. RAU counts an ack only when it matches the current epoch.

common_ports.name: csr_req
common_ports.doc: Address, write data, write enable, from CRU, which owns the CSR fabric. CRU's own csr ports are the host side. Width: address + data + write enable (preliminary address).

common_ports.name: csr_rsp
common_ports.doc: Read data, done. Width: read data + done.

common_ports.name: csr_credit
common_ports.doc: Credit return for the CSR channel.

common_ports.name: clk_gated
common_ports.doc: CCV_CHECK only: the block's clock gate is closed this cycle. An OBSERVATION port, like a channel's `_tid` under CCV_TRACE: it exists for the wake checker in the top's checker bank (Q-33), is read by nothing in the design, and is absent from every synthesis view. What decides to gate stays inside the block.

channel_signals.doc: Asserted ONE CYCLE AHEAD of the payload, on every interface without exception. A credit is consumed when valid asserts, not when the payload lands, and once asserted valid is binding -- the payload follows on schedule even if a stall arrives in between.

The packed struct. Same flop count as valid, so it arrives no later than it otherwise would. A channel may declare LEAD fields (lead_fields): that slice of the same register is written with valid, one cycle ahead of the rest, so on the wire it carries the lead of the message whose valid is up while the rest carries the previous message's payload. The lane mask is the one case today (Q-40).
Stall-invalidate: temporarily invalidates outstanding credits. No message may be sent the cycle after it is received, which makes the in-flight window a fixed count rather than a handshake.

Wake request toward the receiver, asserted by the sender ahead of a send so a gated receiver can ungate. One per channel instance, not per slot, and outside the credit scheme. Replaces the global wake_req common port: wake is directional and per channel, so it belongs in the channel bundle.

channels.name: ccv_fet_dec_instr
channels.doc: Fetched, length-decoded, aligned instruction words, two per warp across all four tier-1 warps. Fetch faults ride here rather than a separate path. On a branch, checkpoint_id names the PC-group checkpoint FET took for it and pred_taken FET's predicted direction (uniform-only first; A-42); both are don't-care on other instructions. A predicted mask replaces pred_taken when divergent prediction lands. GROUP MASK AND EPOCH (A-69, A-70): group_mask is the lanes of the PC group the instruction was fetched for, set by FET, which owns the groups, and carried through DEC to OOE, which needs it at rename (merge elision: is the mask full?) and sends it as issue_mask. fetch_epoch is the warp's epoch when it was fetched: FET takes a new one from every redirect, and DEC and OOE drop any uop whose epoch is not the warp's current one, which is how wrong-path uops still in this channel, in DEC or in the decode queue are discarded after a redirect. FINAL EXIT (AR's and OA's responses TI-27): final_exit marks the exit whose fetch clears the warp's last live lanes. Exit is never predicated, so fetching one exits exactly its group's lanes. A squash that discards an earlier exit discards the mark with it, and the refetched final exit is marked again once FET's mask is restored. ALL_WAITING (TI-40, AR's revs 161-164): On a chwidth it is the chwidth's convergence instead (O-81; ccv_dec_ooe_uop says how OOE takes it): set when the chwidth's group is every live lane, the converged wait's test. Otherwise FET sets it on the instruction whose fetch leaves every live lane of the warp waiting at a barrier: a wait whose group is every live lane (a converged wait, which FET does not park and marks no waiting bits for; OOE holds rename behind it), or an exit by the last group not waiting. OOE starts CCV_DEMOTION_THRESHOLD_BARRIER's timer when the marked uop retires with nothing younger in its warp. DEC passes it through.

slot_attrs_why.slot_binding: four warp streams of two: tier-1 stream = slot / 2
slot_attrs_why.ordering: each stream's two slots are strictly program-ordered
slot_attrs_why.binding_key: the stream a message belongs to, carried so the binding is checked rather than stated: tier1_id must equal slot / binding_group

channels.name: ccv_ooe_fet_decq_credit
channels.doc: Decode-queue credits back to FET, per tier-1 warp (TI-46, form (b), DA tab rev 96; OA's revs 262-268). OOE refuses no uop on ccv_dec_ooe_uop for a per-warp reason: FET holds CCV_P_DECQ_WARP_MAX credits a warp, counted in decode-queue slots, and picks a warp only while they cover the next instruction's slots, which it counts exactly by predecode (DEC asserts the count). credit_count is the slots of the slot's warp that left the decode queue this cycle: those renamed, and those a flush or rewind squashed, in the cycle they are dropped, so FET never resynchronises. An instruction needing more slots than the share borrows, only from full credits, into a 5-bit signed counter (OA's rev 263). HELD-AHEAD: after FET fetches a converged wait it marks all_waiting, the warp fetches at most CCV_P_HELD_AHEAD slots past it and never borrows. released clears that: OOE sets it in the cycle SYU's answer reaches it on ccv_syu_ooe_rel. A rewind beat (a squash of the wait, or a demotion) clears it at FET too. A message is sent for a slot only when credit_count or released is non-zero.
channels.id_classes_why: Credits are counts of slots from several uops, owned by no one transaction; the uops they free are in the trace as they rename.

slot_attrs_why.slot_binding: slot k is tier-1 warp k's return, so every warp's credits return in the cycle they free, whatever the others do
slot_attrs_why.ordering: a warp's returns are one stream, in the order its slots left the queue
slot_attrs_why.binding_key: tier1_id must equal the slot, checked rather than stated

channels.name: ccv_dec_ooe_uop
channels.backpressure: held: OA confirmed (TI-22, OA's rev 136) that the decode queue holds DEC's uops for as long as rename stalls, with no bound of its own (OOE doc, Decode queue: DEC sees a full queue as ordinary credit backpressure). A uop sent against credit is outstanding until rename takes it, so response_within_n holds it to CCV_P_TIMEOUT_BP, a watchdog; the measured maximum age is reported every run (AR's response TI-22)
channels.doc: Format-decoded operations with architectural register names (src_arch holds two sources and src2_arch the third -- Format A's rs2, an independent source such as mad.lo's and dp4's accumulator input; dst_arch is the destination, always), the predicate guard and the predicate destination as separate fields (pred_guard with pred_neg, pred_dst with pred_we: ISA Format C carries them in separate fields, so @P0 setp P1 is one instruction), the immediate and scale enable, six per cycle into the queue ahead of rename. imm is always the architectural immediate: a branch's is its encoded halfword offset from the next instruction, and ilen (the instruction length code, as on ccv_fet_dec_instr) rides beside it, so OOE computes the target as pc + bytes(ilen) + 2 * imm rather than DEC folding the length in (arch open A-8). checkpoint_id and pred_taken pass through from FET on a branch: OOE compares RCU's resolved outcome with pred_taken to detect a mispredict, then names the checkpoint on ccv_ooe_fet_redirect (A-42). sched_attr (A-66): the scheduling attributes, decoded by DEC so OOE never decodes opcode, whose encoding is preliminary and expected to churn. The three fields A-75 asked for (TI-1, agreed by Daniel 2026-10-08), so OOE never decodes opcode: src_valid[3], bit i set when source i is a real read (bits 0 and 1 the two fields of src_arch, bit 2 src2_arch), so OOE renames and waits on nothing else; pred_use[2], how the predicate is read: 0 none, 1 guard (an enable: switched-off lanes keep their old value, so merge_en is set, and a masked load owes its copy), 2 data (sel's selector: no merge); imm_kind[3], what imm holds: 0 a literal, 1 predicate logic's two sources (qualifiers in imm[5:0], [2:0] and [5:3], each [1:0] the architectural predicate and [2] its negate), which OOE renames and rewrites on ccv_ooe_rcu_issue, 2 srd's warp_base identity, 3 srd's ctaid identity, 4 srd #2's %lanectx (ISA v1.9 O-64; OA's response TI-33): ((CCV_P_CORE_ID << CCV_W_WARP_ID) | hardware warp context) << 5, the context being warp_id, which a warp keeps while parked, so its spill space and its O-83 region never move, 5 srd #3's %privoff (ISA v1.9 O-83; DA tab rev 95): 3 * CCV_LANE_CONTEXTS, the O-83 run's offset from local_base in windows, the same on every lane, warp and CTA. OOE substitutes each; the lane ORs its index into 2 and 4, and passes 3 and 5 through. Exit is sched_attr's serial code 3. A guard or data use is never bypassed, and OA adds that pred_use feeds the A-62 late bit. Layout MSB first: bypass_group[3], rs_miu, exec_rcu, cross_lane, writes_gpr, writes_pred, mem_kind[2], branch, serial[3], lat_class[3] (CCV_P_W_SCHED_ATTR has the codes). lat_class sets a producer's full latency; bypass_group, as producer and as consumer, indexes the bypass table, whose penalties are parameters (OI-16, Daniel's responses OA-4). DEC owns the opcode-to-attribute table. mem_op, space and ordering (A-68) are decoded here too, for memory ops, and OOE copies them to ccv_ooe_miu_memop unexamined, so opcode decoding lives only in DEC and MIU stays off the opcode census. DEC never emits mem_op 0xF, which is OOE's bulk discard (A-41); asserted on DEC's output (V-52). mem_op and space are don't-care unless sched_attr's rs_miu is set, as is mem_kind; ordering is reserved zero except on a fence (rs_miu with mem_kind fence), which OOE refuses otherwise (IS-11). group_mask and fetch_epoch pass through from FET (A-69, A-70): OOE renames no uop whose fetch_epoch differs from its warp's current epoch, and every issued uop's issue_mask is the group_mask it arrived with. The mask rides per slot. Sharing it once per warp was considered and dropped (A-72): it saves about 10% of ccv_fet_dec_instr's wires and at most 5% of this channel's, and here it would also need the freely bound slots regrouped by warp and a field shared across a slot group. FAULTS (ISA v1.9 §12; AR's and IS's responses IS-16): cause is the uop's fault cause, CCV_W_FAULT_CAUSE's code: 1 F-FETCH when FET's fetch_fault came with the instruction, else 2 F-ILLEGAL from DEC's own check, else 0. Fetch beats decode, settled here where both are known, and the ROB keeps one cause per entry, the lower code winning (§12.5). F-FORMAT (OI-57, OA's response): OOE stays opcode-blind (A-66), so DEC's table sends the format decoded, not the format code. fmt_rsv has one bit per chwidth code, bit i for code i (0 = 32, 1 = 16, 2 = 8, 3 = 4 bits), set where this op's format code is reserved at that width: codes 10 and 11 at every width, 01 at 32 and 4 bits (ISA v1.9 §4). It is 0 for an op with no format field. fmt_opnd names the operand whose committed width selects the bit: 0 src0, 1 src1, 2 src2, 3 the destination. OOE raises F-FORMAT (cause 4) at rename when fmt_rsv[width(fmt_opnd)] is set, from its committed per-register width table. F-WIDTH needs no field of its own beyond xfer_size and all_waiting (below): a memory access's rdata is the destination for a load and the data source for a store (mem_kind). A store's data source is always src_arch's first register, its base and then its index following it, so OOE takes a store's data register, its width code and its MIU pipes from that first source (AR-24 (d)). final_exit passes through from FET (TI-27): the warp has exited when the uop carrying it retires, so OOE holds no live mask. slot_form and arg_slot (TI-31, AR's response): a memory op in Format D's launch-slot mode (O-45) sets slot_form, and arg_slot is its 4-bit launch slot, an immediate where the base register would be; decoded here and copied by OOE to ccv_ooe_miu_memop unexamined, as mem_op and space are. Zero for every other op. PREDICATE TRANSFERS (TI-36, AR's and OA's responses): DEC cracks ld.pred and st.pred into one uop per predicate of the mask, ascending, uop k moving Pk's word at disp + 4k of the 16-byte frame, mem_op 4 (load) or 5 (store). ld.pred's uop names Pk in pred_dst with pred_we; st.pred's names it in pred_guard with pred_use data (2), never a guard. Each uop is idempotent, so a squash or demotion after a partial retirement re-runs the instruction from its first uop. local_form (IS-19, adopted by DA 2026-10-23; ISA v1.9 O-69; OA's response IS-19): a memory op in Format D's interleaved local mode, ld.local, st.local, ld.pred.local or st.pred.local, sets local_form. It names no base register, so src_valid marks none and OOE renames no base: ld.local's only GPR is its destination, st.local's its data. imm is the unsigned 17-bit byte offset b, and space is global. The predicate forms crack as ld.pred and st.pred do, uop k at b + 4k, mem_op 4 or 5. OOE copies local_form to ccv_ooe_miu_memop unexamined, as slot_form. Zero for every other op. all_waiting passes through from FET (TI-40): on a wait (serial 2) it marks a converged wait, which OOE holds rename behind and reports with held set; on a marked wait or exit it starts the barrier demotion timer at retire. On a chwidth (serial 1, or a chwidth.multi sibling) it means converged instead (O-81, DA tab rev 91): FET sets it when the chwidth's group is every live lane, and DEC copies it to every sibling of a cracked chwidth.multi. A chwidth with it clear raises F-WIDTH at dispatch, precisely and predicate-independently, so a diverged chwidth.multi faults whole at its first sibling. It starts no timer on a chwidth. XFER_SIZE and XFER_SIGNED (O-80, DA tab rev 90; DEC spec rev 13): a sized load or store's transfer, from DEC's table, since OOE never decodes the opcode (A-66). xfer_size is 0 for rdata's width, as before, 1 for one byte or 2 for two. xfer_signed sign-extends a sized load (ld.s8, ld.s16). Both are 0 on every other uop. F-WIDTH gains O-80's case: a sized transfer wider than rdata's committed width faults, that is a byte into nothing narrower than 8 bits, or a halfword into nothing narrower than 16. rdata at 4 bits faults as before, for every memory access. Rename, placement, footprint and the width codes follow rdata's width as ever. SERIAL is 3 bits (TI-41, OA's rev 198): 0 none, 1 chwidth, 2 barrier wait (bar.wait, bar.wait.phase), 3 exit, 4 barrier arrive (bar.arrive: no rename hold, reported at retire), 5-7 spare.

slot_attrs_why.ordering: six uops from up to four warps have no total order; order is per warp

channels.name: ccv_ooe_rcu_issue
channels.doc: What the scheduler selected: physical register names (three sources; the guard predicate and the predicate destination separately, with pred_we saying whether a predicate is written), opcode, element width, the issue group's lane mask, and the ALU immediate, which RCU substitutes into an operand slot at register read so lanes never see an immediate. One slot per select resource (CCV_ISSUE_RESOURCES = 9): S0-S3, P0-P3, R; see SECTIONED LANES below. MERGE (A-33): with merge_en set (the issue mask is not full or the op is guarded), phys_old_dst is a fourth source, read at issue with the others and carried to the lane as merge_data, so it bypasses like any operand; the lane writes its inactive lanes from it. merge_en = 0 makes phys_old_dst don't-care. Predicates merge in RCU instead: at write-back RCU read-modify-writes the 32-bit row from phys_pred_old_dst (A-43). A masked load sends a second, copy-only op here, opcode CCV_OP_PRF_COPY = 0x1FF, with the load's rob_tag: it writes only the load's inactive lanes (GPR and predicate destination alike) and produces no done (A-38). Fixed latency: once RCU accepts an issue the result lands at the contracted latency, and there is no port grant (Q-51, A-28). ZERO REGISTERS (A-64): CCV_P_PHYS_ZERO and CCV_P_PRED_ZERO, one past each pool, read zero and are never written. A read of one needs no PRF port: RCU decodes the index and drives a constant, which matters because a launched warp's early reads all name them (A-73). A launched warp's sources, guard and old destinations may name them; phys_dst, phys_pred_dst and the destinations of every write never do. PREDICATE LOGIC (TI-1): pand, por and pxor read two predicates, and OOE renames them like any source, so imm carries their physical names, not DEC's qualifiers: [CCV_P_W_PHYS_PRED-1:0] the first source, [CCV_P_W_PHYS_PRED] its negate, then the second source and its negate, 2 (CCV_P_W_PHYS_PRED + 1) = 14 bits. RCU reads them as it reads phys_pred_guard, so the issue channel does not grow. SECTIONED LANES (Daniel's responses OI-28 to OI-31, change doc 'Interface spec changes -- sectioned lanes', TI-9): a lane is four 8-bit sections and the PRF four section banks; a register name is a row (phys_src, phys_src2, phys_dst, phys_old_dst) plus a position (src_pos, dst_pos, old_dst_pos), each operand with its own width code (src_width; dst_width, which the merge source shares, being the same architectural register). footprint is the op's 4-bit mask: lane sections for an op on S0-S3 (the union of its operands' sections, widened to CCV_FOOT_MIN for its bypass_group; a non-contiguous mask is legal), MIU pipes for a memop on P0-P3, 0 on R. An op sits in its footprint's lowest slot; every other slot of its footprint carries cont = 1 and the same rob_tag, and nothing else. A memop takes P slots here, for RCU to read its operands at its width and position, as well as its pipe footprint on ccv_ooe_miu_memop. Co-issued footprints are disjoint (V-60), so at most one full-width lane op, one full-width memop and one RCU op issue in a cycle, and four 8-bit ops of each. The zero register is valid at any position. bypass_group rides with the op for the lanes' forwarding (OI-16).

slot_attrs_why.slot_binding: slot k is select resource k, CCV_ISSUE_RESOURCES in all: the lane sections S0-S3, the MIU pipes P0-P3, then the RCU unit R. An op sits in its lowest resource's slot and marks every other resource of its footprint continuation, so RCU sees which sections and pipes each cycle's ops hold; free slots would hide that
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: once RCU accepts an issue, the result lands exactly at its contracted latency; OOE schedules wakeup from that and has no grant or late signal to learn otherwise (A-47, Q-51)

channels.name: ccv_rcu_lane_ops
channels.note: Fans out to 32 LANE instances; the payload is per-lane.
channels.lead_why: The mask gates the lane, so it must arrive before what it gates (Q-40): section_en (an op holds the section) and sec_pred_bit (this lane computes it) are the lane's valid, per section and per lane, sent with valid one cycle ahead of the operands, so a masked-off or empty section never clocks its operand capture or its datapath. Nothing else leads (Daniel, 2026-10-18): a lead is captured in valid's cycle, so at the lane and at a repeated link's first stage it is a flop written every cycle, against the module's ungated allowance, and a lead is kept only for an enable or a real IPC gain. sec_owner and sec_pred_data gate nothing and travel with the operands.
channels.doc: Operands and control to one lane, one message a cycle (Daniel's response OI-28; change doc 'Interface spec changes -- sectioned lanes'). A lane is four 8-bit sections, S0-S3, and up to four ops share the message, each in its own sections. operand (three 32-bit ports, src0-src2) and merge_data (the fourth) are the four operand ports, 32 bits a lane: one byte a section, each from its own section bank. Per section: section_en (an op holds it), sec_owner (the lead section, its lowest, of the op that holds it; a section is its op's lead where sec_owner names itself), sec_opcode, sec_pred_bit and sec_pred_data. An owner rather than a lead bit, because a footprint may be non-contiguous (AR-15): ops on {S0, S2} and {S1, S3} share a message, and a lead bit alone cannot say whose S2 is (TI-10). On a lead section only: each of the four operands' position and width (sec_opnd_pos, sec_opnd_width) and the destination's (sec_dst_pos, sec_dst_width). The op routes bytes freely within its footprint as part of executing, the swizzle, after the bypass mux; it never reaches another lane's word, which only a warp-collective in RCU moves. A full-width op holds all four sections. sec_pred_bit is the section op's ENABLE in this lane: issue mask AND guard, the same computation as active_mask. A section whose enable is clear does not compute: its op returns merge_data's bytes as its result, which is how a masked or guarded write keeps its inactive lanes' old values under rename (A-33, A-44); merge_data is don't-care when the op's merge_en is 0. For CCV_OP_PRF_COPY an enabled lane's result is don't-care: RCU writes only the inactive lanes. sec_pred_data is a predicate read as DATA, e.g. sel's selector. What reaches a lane: every opcode with a per-lane input, a GPR or the lane's own hardwired index (Q-32, Q-38). RCU executes the opcodes whose inputs are all warp-level -- predicate logic, pmov, movi, movi48, branch resolution -- plus the horizontal ops (shfl, vote, ballot, unballot). setp, add.pp and cas run in lanes although they write predicates; sec_pred_out carries those back. srd runs in the lane: selector 0 ORs the lane's index into the warp_base immediate, selector 1 passes %ctaid through, decoded from the selector by DEC as two opcodes. operand_byp is the lane-local bypass (A-59, TI-8, TI-9): one CCV_P_W_LANE_BYP_SEL select per operand port per section, since co-issued narrow ops may each forward from a different producer. A select with its forward bit set replaces that section's byte of that port with a result this lane computed earlier, named by the producer's lead section and its age, the cycles between the two messages' arrival here less CCV_LAT_LANE_BYP. RCU sets it for a source whose lane producer has not yet written the PRF, which only a dependant woken at a bypass offset can meet. The selects are the same on every lane, like the opcodes. LAYOUT: every per-section field packs S0 at its LSBs. sec_opnd_pos, sec_opnd_width and operand_byp hold one entry per port per section, section-major: entry k * (CCV_L_OPERANDS_PER_LANE + 1) + i is section k's port i, ports src0-src2 then merge_data. sec_opnd_pos, sec_opnd_width, sec_dst_pos and sec_dst_width are read on lead sections only.

slot_attrs_why.lockstep: the 32 lanes are one SIMD datapath: they advance together, with no per-lane flow control
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: the lane pipeline is part of the contracted lane latency; a lane that stalled would slip every dependant OOE has already scheduled (A-47)

channels.name: ccv_lane_rcu_res
channels.doc: One lane's results, one message a cycle (OI-28): a 32-bit result, used whole by a full-width op and by section for narrow ones, already steered to each destination's position inside the lane; per section, sec_valid (an op's result is here), sec_pred_out (setp's compare, add.pp's predicate: one bit a lane per op, on the op's lead section). RCU knows which op held which section, the lane latency being fixed, so no tag rides here. RCU writes the PRF by slice through per-lane write enables: every lane for an ordinary op (an inactive lane's result is its merge_data), only the inactive lanes for CCV_OP_PRF_COPY (A-44).

slot_attrs_why.lockstep: the 32 lanes are one SIMD datapath: they advance together, with no per-lane flow control
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: lane results land in the PRF at the contracted cycle; RCU never holds one (A-47)

channels.name: ccv_rcu_ooe_done
channels.doc: Completion back to the ROB for arithmetic -- and branch resolution: the condition is a predicate, which lives in RCU's file, so RCU resolves. branch_mask (issue mask AND guard) is what makes a branch divergence rather than a jump; branch_taken is any lane taking it. CCV_OP_PRF_COPY produces no done: its masked load keeps one rob_tag and one completion, the load's (A-38). Nor does any memop: a load or store completes on ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl alone, and RCU, which sends its address and writes a load's data, sends nothing here for it (OI-4, Daniel 2026-10-08). A done for a memop would spend a transfer and, arriving late, could match a reused rob_tag. CCV_DONE_SLOTS slots, a free pool (TI-9, OA's response 2026-10-09): dones arrive at fixed latency from ops issued in different cycles, so they stack by latency class. Four narrow lane ops issued at t - 7, an SFU op at t - 12, an RCU-only op at t - 3 and a warp-collective at t - 5 all land at t: seven. A lane op's done leaves the cycle its write lands, at V-35's bound with no slack, so none can wait for a slot. Memops send none (OI-4). No fault rides here: no cause of ISA v1.9 (§12) originates in RCU or a lane (AR's response IS-16), so exec_fault, fault_lane_mask and the lanes' sec_fault were removed. AR-24 (b), OA's revs 222, 223, 226: branch_mask is issue mask AND guard for a branch and for a barrier arrive, wait and wait.phase. For a ret, aux is the lowest active lane's rs (the target's offset in the ret's 4 GiB code window, ISA section 3) and branch_mask the active lanes whose rs equals it; OOE redirects those lanes to {PC[47:32] of the ret, aux} with stay = 1, and the ret re-issues for the rest, a pass per distinct target. For wait.phase, aux carries ps's lane bits, each lane's expected phase. Don't-care otherwise.

slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: completion at the contracted cycle is what OOE retires against; no late or cancel bit exists (A-47)
slot_attrs_why.distinct_key: at most one done per ROB entry a cycle (OA's rev 279, OI-85): ooe_rob's done count then decrements by one or none, so no adder sits on the retire window's path. Two RCU rows of one entry finishing together (an atomic's A2 and its second slot's copy, or a copy beside its op) are the only case, and RCU holds the second a cycle

channels.name: ccv_rcu_miu_addr
channels.doc: Address operands and store data for memory operations, and active_mask: issue mask AND guard predicate, computed by RCU, the one block holding both. The widest interface in the design. A predicate transfer (mem_op 4 or 5, TI-36) takes its one address from lane 0's base_per_lane whether or not lane 0 is active (O-62), and a predicate store's word, the predicate's 32 bits from RCU's predicate file, rides in store_data's lane 0 slot; active_mask is the issue mask, the merge mask. base_per_lane (TI-32, AR's response): each lane's base register, since only ld.pred and st.pred require a warp-uniform rbase (section 3); an O-30 frame pointer differs on every lane. A slot-form memop (slot_form on ccv_ooe_miu_memop) has no base register: base_per_lane is don't-care, and MIU takes the window from the CTA's launch block. SECTIONED (OI-33): base, index and store data are read at the memop's width and position, a slice, right-aligned in their fields; memop reads use their own PRF ports, never a lane port (CCV_PRF_MEMOP_READ_BITS).

channels.name: ccv_miu_rcu_data
channels.doc: Load return data written into the register file. active_mask (echoing rcu_miu_addr's) gates the write: an inactive lane keeps its old value. pred_result carries a per-lane predicate the memory op produces (cas's success), for RCU's predicate file. phys_dst and phys_pred echo the memop's, so RCU writes back without state: load_data to phys_dst, pred_result (cas's success) to phys_pred. pred_we, set by MIU from the op (cas, not a load), says whether pred_result is written at all -- without it a stateless RCU would clobber the predicate phys_pred names on every load. An L1 hit's data lands at the contracted cycle, with its completion (A-47). A predicate load (mem_op 4, TI-36) returns its word as pred_result with pred_we, and phys_dst the zero register (CCV_P_PHYS_ZERO), which no write reaches: it writes no GPR. Its copy-only op merges the predicate's inactive lanes in RCU. A masked load's inactive lanes are written by its copy-only op through a lane, never by MIU, so this channel carries no merge fields (A-33). SECTIONED (OI-29, OI-33): phys_dst is a row, dst_pos and dst_width the slice the load writes; load_data carries the slice right-aligned in each lane's 32 bits.

slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: L1-hit data must be in the PRF at the contracted cycle, since dependants woken at hit latency read it (A-47)

channels.name: ccv_ooe_miu_memop
channels.doc: The memory operation itself: space, ordering, element width, CTA slot for bounds checking, and the displacement and scale enable the AGU needs (the shift is derived from chwidth). issue_mask is the issue group's lanes before the guard; the lanes that may access memory or fault are rcu_miu_addr.active_mask, which only RCU can compute. phys_dst and phys_pred are the write-back destinations (phys_pred is the uop's pred_dst, renamed), which MIU echoes on ccv_miu_rcu_data so RCU holds no table of outstanding loads. BULK DISCARD (A-41): mem_op 0xF discards every store of warp_id whose ROB index lies in the circular range (branch, tail]: rob_tag names the mispredicted branch and discard_tail, an overlay on disp, the warp's ROB tail, the youngest allocated entry inclusive. Every other field is reserved and zero. It is a command, not a memop: it gets no completion (A-53), the stores it discards still complete individually, and it is never sent in the same cycle as a memop of the same warp. mem_op, space and ordering arrive from DEC on ccv_dec_ooe_uop and pass through OOE unexamined (A-68); 0xF alone is OOE's own. mem_op 4 and 5 are a predicate transfer's uop (TI-36): MIU forms one address from lane 0, a load returns its word as pred_result, and a store completes at execute and drains after commit as a read-merge-write of its word, new = (old & ~m) | (d & m), m the address message's active_mask (MIU spec rev 25). SECTIONED (OI-33): pipes is the memop's footprint over MIU's pipes P0-P3, four at 32 bits, two at 16 and one at 8, at its data position; phys_dst is a row and dst_pos its position, echoed for the slice write-back. LOADS IN THE BULK DISCARD (AR's and OA's responses TI-21): the discard covers the warp's uncommitted loads in its range as well as its stores, each completed with status replay (ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl). A demotion's squash sends one for warp_id, whatever it holds, and drained waits only for the discarded loads' replay completions. A demotion's range is the whole ROB, branch == tail, which no other discard sends, since a mispredict's range is never empty. A discard of an empty ROB names no instruction and carries id class none; every memop carries instr, which MIU checks. LAUNCH-SLOT FORM (TI-31, AR's response; ISA O-45): slot_form set, the address is (window << 16) + (index << scale) + disp, where the window is the 32-bit word at launch_block_addr + 32 + 8 x arg_slot (ccv_rau_miu_cta). MIU keeps each CTA slot's sixteen windows in a table, filled a line at a time on first use: a memop whose window is not yet valid is an L1 miss, and completes as one. The table's valid bits clear on the slot's ccv_rau_miu_cta and on a kill; the windows are invariant within a launch (section 5.2, F-RO). F-RO, F-ADDR and F-ALIGN apply to the formed address as to any other. arg_slot is 4 bits, sixteen slots (OffArgs + 8k, k < 16). INTERLEAVED LOCAL FORM (IS-19, adopted by DA 2026-10-23; ISA v1.9 O-69): local_form set, disp is the unsigned byte offset b, and lane l's address is ((local_base + CCV_LANE_CONTEXTS) << 16) + (ctx << 22) + 128 x (b / 4) + 4l + b mod 4. local_base is the launch block's word at byte 24, which MIU's per-CTA table holds from the first line it already fills for the launch-slot form, on the same valid bit; ctx is the warp's hardware context, (CCV_P_CORE_ID << CCV_W_WARP_ID) | warp_id, which MIU forms itself, so no field carries it (OA's proposal IS-19). Word w of every lane's frame is one 128-byte line. A predicate transfer in this form (mem_op 4 or 5) is warp-scoped: its one address is the formula's with l = 0. base_per_lane is don't-care. F-ADDR, F-ALIGN and F-RO apply to the formed address. SIZED (O-80, DA tab rev 90; MIU spec rev 38): xfer_size and xfer_signed pass through from ccv_dec_ooe_uop. A nonzero xfer_size is the transfer, one byte (1) or two (2), and 0 leaves it at chwidth, rdata's width, as before. scale_en scales the index by the transfer size, and alignment (O-58) is the transfer's. A sized load's bytes are zero-extended, or sign-extended under xfer_signed, to chwidth before they leave on ccv_miu_rcu_data, which RCU writes at its dst_width as ever. A sized store moves rdata's low bytes.

overlays.name: discard_tail
overlays.doc: The warp's ROB tail on a bulk discard: displacement is AGU-only and dead on a discard, and unlike phys_dst or phys_pred it is not a register name that conservation checkers would misread (A-41).

channels.name: ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl
channels.note: One struct covering completion and faults together; miss notification rides the same path and is the primary demotion trigger.
channels.doc: Completion, replay, fault and MLC miss. The miss indication is the primary demotion trigger, which is why it rides the completion path rather than its own channel. Every memop MIU accepts gets exactly one completion, including a store later bulk-discarded; the bulk-discard command itself gets none (A-41, A-53). An L1 hit completes at exactly CCV_LAT_L1_HIT; no completion at that cycle is the miss indication. Past L1 nothing is contracted, and scratchpad loads and atomics never wake dependants speculatively (A-46). ATOMIC PASSES (AR-21, OA's response): an atomic is A1 (atomic-read), A2 (the lane op) and A3 (atomic-write) under one rob_tag. MIU runs its lanes in passes, at most one lane per address in ascending lane order, and never waits for a line while holding another (V-72). A3's completion carries more = 1 while lanes remain, and OOE re-issues the three steps; more is 0 on every other completion. FAULTS (ISA v1.9 §12.5-12.6): on a faulting completion, cause is the highest-priority cause among the faulting lanes (F-ALIGN, F-ADDR, F-SHARED or F-RO, codes 5-8), address the lowest faulting lane's effective address, and lane_mask the faulting lanes; CRU's record takes exactly those. STATUS: 0 complete, 1 fault (cause and address carry the detail), 2 replay. REPLAY DRAIN (AR's and OA's responses TI-21, MIU spec rev 18): a load a bulk discard covers is completed at once with status replay, and MIU orphans its requests to DCU: their responses are dropped, with no write on ccv_miu_rcu_data after the completion (a data beat already started finishes first, and its completion may then carry its real status), no hint on ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl_hint, and its fill notice ignored. A discard that races a normal completion in the same cycle still yields exactly one completion (A-41). So a demotion's drain waits for no fill.

slot_attrs_why.ordering: genuinely out of order across four pipes
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: an L1 hit completes at exactly the contracted cycle and no completion then is the miss indication (A-46), which only means something if OOE never delays taking a completion (A-47)

channels.name: ccv_ooe_miu_retire
channels.doc: Commit or discard for the store buffer, so stores leave only after their instruction retires.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_fet_redirect
channels.doc: A mispredicted branch: the warp, its tier-1 stream, the branch's checkpoint, the lanes that took it, the target PC, and a fetch epoch so FET can discard in-flight fetches from the wrong path. RCU resolves (the condition is a predicate) and OOE compares the outcome with the prediction (pred_taken, A-42); OOE redirects only on a mispredict, at rate 1, serialising them deliberately (A-6). FET owns the PC-group state: it holds a checkpoint of it per unresolved branch (CCV_P_BR_CKPTS) and rebuilds the groups itself from checkpoint_id plus taken_mask, so OOE no longer resends group masks it does not own. Fixed latency (A-58): FET applies a redirect the cycle it lands and never stalls it, because ccv_ooe_fet_ckpt_free is latency-matched to this channel and the pair's arrival order must be its send order; FET applies a redirect before any free landing the same cycle. EPOCH OWNERSHIP (A-70, A-74): OOE owns every warp's fetch epoch and is the only block that advances it: on each redirect, on ccv_rau_ooe_demote, and on a kill. It tells FET of every change on this channel. A redirect carries the new epoch; a demotion or kill sends an epoch notice, epoch_only = 1, for which FET only takes fetch_epoch for warp_id, and checkpoint_id, taken_mask and target_pc are don't-care (no restore, no PC change, no checkpoint freed). FET advances nothing itself. It tags everything it fetches for the warp afterwards with that epoch on ccv_fet_dec_instr. Both blocks hold the epoch per warp_id, not per tier-1 slot, so it survives demotion and restore. Neither resets it at launch, because a relaunched warp_id could meet its predecessor's uops still in flight. The channel is fixed-latency and in order, so notices and redirects for a warp land in the order sent, and V-56 holds: one channel latency after every change, FET's epoch for a warp equals OOE's. REWIND (AR's and OA's responses TI-24 (3); FET spec, demotion rewind): on a demotion, after the epoch notice and the drain (CCV_DRAIN_WAIT), OOE sends one beat per group it holds, epoch_only = 1 and rewind = 1, naming in taken_mask the lanes whose oldest unretired entry, in the ROB or the decode queue, is at target_pc. FET sets those lanes' PCs to it; a lane in no beat keeps FET's PC, exact because the drain left nothing of it in flight, and min-PC merges what now coincides. checkpoint_id and fetch_epoch are don't-care on a beat. OOE sends ccv_ooe_rau_drained only once its last beat has landed in FET, at its send cycle plus this channel's fixed latency, so FET migrates the rewound PCs. A replayable fault (IS-4) uses the same beats. Here rather than a channel of its own: the beats need nothing the notice does not carry but one bit, and the fixed latency and order that make the notice safe. REWIND AND WAITS (TI-40, AR's rev 164, FET spec rev 22): a demotion's rewind beat of a warp OOE holds behind a converged wait sets rewind_held, and held_long gives that wait's length (0 16 bits, 1 32), so FET sets the beat's lanes to its PC less that length, back to the wait, which retired. FET rewinds its waiting lanes too: one named in no beat goes back by its own long bit; one named in a plain beat takes the beat's PC. OWN_PC (OA's rev 226, AR's rev 176, FET spec rev 24): set on a rewind_held beat when the held warp has no unretired uop, in the ROB or the decode queue. FET then rewinds the beat's lanes from its own PC, less the wait's length, and ignores target_pc. That is exact because the drain left nothing fetched past the wait, so OOE stores no PC for the case. FET asserts that an own_pc beat's lanes form one of its groups. 0 on every other beat. STAY (AR-24 (b), AR's rev 172, OA's rev 223, FET spec rev 23): set on every ret redirect. The branch's active lanes not in taken_mask stay at the ret's own PC rather than its fall-through, so the ret re-issues for them with their own targets. 0 on every other redirect.

slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: A-58: latency-matched with ccv_ooe_fet_ckpt_free; if FET could stall a redirect, a free sent after it could be applied before it and release a checkpoint the redirect is restoring.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_fet_ckpt_free

slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: A-56: one bitmap frees any number of checkpoints, so FET can always take it the cycle it lands; a stalled free would hold a checkpoint FET could reuse.

channels.latency_match_why: A-58: a free that overtook a redirect could release a checkpoint FET had already reallocated. Equal link stages and receivers that apply on landing make arrival order equal send order, and FET applies a redirect before frees in the same cycle.
channels.doc: Checkpoints freed by a correct branch resolution (A-56). One bit per tier-1 slot per checkpoint, bit tier1_id*CCV_P_BR_CKPTS + checkpoint_id; a set bit frees that checkpoint in FET. One message frees any number across all warps, so nothing queues: OOE sends whenever the mask is non-zero. A checkpoint is freed exactly once: here on a correct resolution, or by FET itself when a redirect restores it (FET frees the restored checkpoint and every younger one of that warp) or a demotion or kill resets the warp. OOE never frees a checkpoint the same cycle's redirect squashes, and drops the resolutions of squashed branches (A-58). Every set bit must name a checkpoint live in FET when it lands (V-46). Branches resolve out of order, which is why FET cannot infer frees from a count.

channels.name: ccv_miu_spm_req
channels.doc: Scratchpad access with a per-bank address set: one pass, at most one word in each bank, which bank_addr names, with write_data and byte_mask laid out by bank (bank b at bytes 4b to 4b + 3). MIU splits a warp's access into passes, one for each distinct word a bank holds for it, its lanes in ascending order, so a store's highest lane wins a word that lanes share, as ccv-sim's does. SPM's resolver issues one pass a cycle, and reports the cycles a pass waited for it as conflict_serialization (SPM spec rev 2; TI's rev 230). spm_op 0 reads and 1 writes, under byte_mask. byte_mask is already ANDed with the instruction's active_mask: a predicated-off lane's bytes are never enabled, so SPM needs no lane mask of its own (arch open A-20; an MIU assertion when MIU is RTL).

channels.name: ccv_spm_miu_rsp
channels.doc: Scratchpad read data plus how many extra cycles conflicts cost, which the timing model needs.

channels.name: ccv_miu_dcu_req
channels.backpressure: pending: a memory-path request, whose receiver holds it only while its miss buffers are full behind a memory stall, the backpressured class (AR's response TI-22). It takes the class, and CCV_P_TIMEOUT_BP, when DCU's owner states the hold; until then CCV_P_TIMEOUT_N, which holds only while memory is a fixed-latency stub
channels.doc: Cache access, physically addressed, with the exclusive-ownership request for atomics, and the store data with its byte mask.

channels.name: ccv_dcu_miu_rsp
channels.doc: Cache read data, hit indication and whether ownership was granted, and mlc_miss: the fill that served this access missed in MLC (ccv_mlc_dcu_rsp.miss, passed through). MIU reports it on ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl, since an MLC miss is the primary demotion trigger; without this field the signal stopped at DCU (arch open A-9).

channels.name: ccv_dcu_mlc_req
channels.backpressure: pending: a memory-path request, whose receiver holds it only while its miss buffers are full behind a memory stall, the backpressured class (AR's response TI-22). It takes the class, and CCV_P_TIMEOUT_BP, when MLC's owner states the hold; until then CCV_P_TIMEOUT_N, which holds only while memory is a fixed-latency stub
channels.doc: Fills and writebacks from L1 to the shared cache, tagged with core ID.

channels.name: ccv_mlc_dcu_rsp
channels.doc: Line fills and ownership grants back to L1.

channels.name: ccv_mlc_dcu_probe
channels.note: A wake source: the D-cache cannot sleep through an inbound probe.
channels.doc: Inbound invalidate or downgrade. Unsolicited, and a wake source, since a sleeping D-cache must still answer.

channels.name: ccv_dcu_mlc_probe_ack
channels.doc: Probe response, carrying dirty data when the line was modified.

channels.name: ccv_fet_mlc_ifill
channels.backpressure: pending: a memory-path request, whose receiver holds it only while its miss buffers are full behind a memory stall, the backpressured class (AR's response TI-22). It takes the class, and CCV_P_TIMEOUT_BP, when MLC's owner states the hold; until then CCV_P_TIMEOUT_N, which holds only while memory is a fixed-latency stub
channels.doc: Instruction cache miss straight to MLC, bypassing the D-cache. Physically addressed, so no ASID (arch open A-5).

channels.name: ccv_mlc_fet_ifill_rsp
channels.doc: Instruction line fill.

channels.name: ccv_miu_fet_itlb
channels.doc: Walker returning an ITLB entry.

channels.name: ccv_fet_miu_itlb_req
channels.doc: Fetch asking the walker for a translation on an ITLB miss: the virtual PAGE number (CCV_W_VA - CCV_L_PAGE_SHIFT bits), so no meaningless low bits can disagree with the TLB tag (arch open A-4).
channels.outstanding_why: FET has at most one ITLB miss outstanding, which makes a correlation tag unnecessary: code is a handful of pages, the ITLB is 4-8 entries, and fetch stalls on a miss anyway. Asserted (ccv_common_chk_outstanding), not tagged. Revisit if multi-warp fetch across distant code regions proves otherwise.

channels.name: ccv_mlc_exb_req
channels.backpressure: pending: a memory-path request, whose receiver holds it only while its miss buffers are full behind a memory stall, the backpressured class (AR's response TI-22). It takes the class, and CCV_P_TIMEOUT_BP, when EXB's owner states the hold; until then CCV_P_TIMEOUT_N, which holds only while memory is a fixed-latency stub
channels.doc: The protocol-neutral outbound request. Everything the core knows about coherence is expressed here.

channels.name: ccv_exb_mlc_rsp
channels.doc: Protocol-neutral inbound: fills and grants, matched to their request by req_id, and probes, which carry their line address and what they ask. probe_type is the discriminator: 0 is a response; non-zero is a probe, on which req_id, line_data, ownership_grant and miss are reserved and zero, so an overloaded field is checkable rather than 'meaningless' (arch open A-10).

channels.name: ccv_exb_ext_out
channels.note: The coherent boundary, meant to be THE ONE EXCEPTION: TileLink TL-C, obeying that protocol's rules rather than ours, contained in a bridge block so the exception stays at a single port. NOT YET (arch opens A-11, A-24): today this and ccv_ext_exb_in are ordinary credited channels whose payload is a flattened TL-C bundle, with one valid per TL channel and no TL ready. The outer credit is the only back-pressure, so a blocked TL channel stalls all of them, and TL-C's freedom from deadlock rests on some channels never being blocked by others. The bundle cannot express that, so nothing run against it says anything about TL-C deadlock behaviour. It is a stand-in for S1's single core and in-order testbench memory; per-channel ready/valid replaces it in EXB's session (Q-36).
channels.doc: TileLink TL-C, outbound: channels A (acquire/get/put), C (release, probe response) and E (grant ack). The core is a master. How it decomposes -- flattened bundle or separate TL channels -- is EXB session work.

channels.name: ccv_rau_fet_launch
channels.doc: A warp becoming resident: where to start, what code it may touch, which address space, which CTA slot. tier1_id is the tier-1 slot RAU placed the warp in (A-65): FET fetches it in that slot's binding group on ccv_fet_dec_instr and indexes its checkpoints by it, as OOE does from ccv_rau_ooe_alloc. live_mask (AR's response TI-27 (a)) is the warp's lanes, which FET picks among: lanes [0, n) with n = min(32, T - 32 x warp_in_cta), T the CTA's thread count from the grid descriptor (Q-50). A partial warp is always the low lanes (ISA section 5.3). 32 bits rather than a count, since a restore's mask on ccv_pca_fet_mig is arbitrary and FET loads one register from either.

channels.name: ccv_rau_ooe_alloc
channels.doc: What RAU tells OOE about a warp's residency (A-64, A-65). alloc_op: 0 free, 1 launch, 2 restore-allocate, 3 restore-activate. Launch: OOE maps the warp's 16 architectural GPRs and 4 predicates to the hardwired zero registers (CCV_P_PHYS_ZERO, CCV_P_PRED_ZERO), so no zeroing traffic is sent and the warp may issue at once. Restore-allocate, before the PCA transfer: OOE allocates 16 GPRs and 4 predicates from the slot's reservation, so it never waits, and sends ccv_ooe_rcu_map with direction 1. Restore-activate, after ccv_pca_rau_mig_done: only now may the warp rename and issue. A single activation message would deadlock, since PCA's rows need the map and the map would need the activation. Free: the warp's state is released. tier1_id is the tier-1 slot RAU placed the warp in; OOE keeps its warp-to-slot table from it, which indexes the ROB, rob_tag's slot field, the per-slot reservations and the checkpoint-free bitmap, so ccv_dec_ooe_uop needs no slot field. Identity: ctaid and warp_in_cta, which OOE shadows so it can put srd's value in the immediate at issue (Q-38, A-25). RAU allocates no physical registers: OOE's global free lists do, from a reservation held per tier-1 slot whether occupied or not, so activation never waits and no credit is withheld (A-30, A-49). RAU's table is indexed by warp slot, which does not change while a warp parks, so identity stays out of the parked context by design. BARRIERS (IS-16, ISA v1.9 O-59): on a launch and on a restore-allocate, barrier_count is the warp's CTA's allocated barrier count, 0 to 16. OOE holds it in the tier-1 slot's state and raises F-BARRIER at dispatch for a barrier instruction whose ID is at or above it, so a faulting reference never reaches SYU. It rides restore-allocate too because a restored warp can land in a different slot, and RAU, which owns the CTA's allocation, is the one holder that survives demotion (OA's response IS-16). CTA SLOT (TI-34, AR's and OA's responses): on a launch and on a restore-allocate, cta_slot is the CTA slot RAU gave the warp's CTA. OOE holds it per tier-1 slot, beside barrier_count, and stamps it onto ccv_ooe_miu_memop, ccv_ooe_syu_bar and ccv_ooe_cru_fault, whose per-CTA state (F-SHARED's and F-RO's bounds, the launch-slot windows, SYU's barrier counts) is indexed by it. A parked warp keeps its CTA slot at RAU, so a restore-allocate carries it again and nothing migrates. Don't-care on free and restore-activate.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_rau_status
channels.doc: Per-warp stall and progress reporting, feeding demotion policy -- and fault_taken, the fault path to RAU: OOE raises it at retirement with the warp_id, and RAU kills every warp of the context: with one resident context (the ASID field's contract), every valid warp context, resident and parked, with no lookup, and it stops every queued launch (DA's response IS-2, 2026-10-20: a fatal fault terminates the context, not the grid). The host's kill_grid on ccv_cru_rau_cfg stays grid-scoped: it is a request, not a fault. CRU records the fault in parallel (ccv_ooe_cru_fault) for the host, and is not on the path that stops execution. EXITED (AR's response TI-24 (2), OA's rev 149): a level, set once the warp's C_EXIT has retired and the warp holds no ROB entry, deferred-free or squashed-pending slot included, and no memop outstanding at MIU, the kill's quiesce; held until RAU frees the slot (alloc_op 0). RAU then frees the tier-1 slot, and on a CTA's last warp the CTA's scratchpad, barrier entries and CTA slot. A committed store still draining is never matched by rob_tag or warp_id again (MIU spec), so both may be reused.

channels.name: ccv_rau_ooe_demote
channels.doc: The order to squash a warp to its retirement boundary and report where to resume.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_rau_drained
channels.doc: Confirmation that only architectural state remains, with the resume PC. Migration may begin. OOE sends it only once the epoch notice it sent for the demotion (epoch_only on ccv_ooe_fet_redirect, A-74) has landed in FET, at its send cycle plus that channel's fixed latency, the same rule as its kill_ack. The guarantee that a restored warp is never fetched under an epoch older than OOE's (V-57) is then explicit rather than resting on the migration handshake's length. Every demote gets exactly one drained. REFUSED (OA's response TI-25 (2)): a demote that lands after the warp's exit has retired is refused, with no squash, no map and no rewind beats, and drained carries refused = 1; RAU cancels the demotion (no migration commands), and exited frees the slot as for any finishing warp. A demote that lands before the exit retires is an ordinary demotion, and the squash takes the exit with it.

channels.name: ccv_rau_rcu_mig
channels.doc: Which warp and direction a migration moves. RCU pairs it with ccv_ooe_rcu_map by warp_id and direction and proceeds once both have arrived, in either order; at most one migration per warp is in flight (A-45).

channels.name: ccv_ooe_rcu_map
channels.doc: Where a migrating warp's architectural registers live: its RAT, 16 physical GPR names and 4 physical predicate names. Physical locations exist only in OOE's RAT, so this replaces RAU's prf_base + arch addressing. direction 0: demote, RCU reads the named rows out to PCA; 1: restore, RCU writes PCA's rows into them. RCU pairs it with ccv_rau_rcu_mig by warp and direction (A-45), and ccv_ooe_rau_drained is sent only after it. Rate 1, separate from the issue channel, whose nine resource slots bind the machine's width. A message is one whole map, atomic and ordered by construction on a single slot, so no slot attributes are declared (the schema refuses them on a rate-1 channel). A demotion map may name the zero registers (A-64): RCU then reads zeros out to PCA. A restore map never does: restore-allocate allocates every register it names. SECTIONED (OI-29, TI-9): a register is a row, a position and a width, so gpr_pos and gpr_width ride beside gpr_map. Rows are warp-private, so demotion and restore move whole rows (OA's response TI-9 (2)). One row per architectural register (AR's and OA's responses TI-25 (1)): Ra moves as mig_row a, R0 to R15 and then the predicate row, 17 rows whatever the map shares, with no merging of shared or zero rows; a register naming the zero register moves a row of zeros. A restore map gives each register a row of its own, and RCU writes row a into Ra's. OOE keeps each register's position and committed width per warp while it is parked (64 bits a warp) and restores them on the restore map. Sharing and zero elision are deferred (PF-40).

channels.name: ccv_rcu_pca_mig
channels.doc: Architectural state out to the parked array on demotion, one 1024-bit row per message. Rows 0 to 15 are the 16 GPRs; rows 16 and up carry the warp's predicate state (CCV_W_PRED_STATE bits, ceil(CCV_W_PRED_STATE / CCV_W_DATA) rows, one today). Addressed: warp_id and mig_row say where the row goes, so PCA places it from the data itself rather than inferring placement from a command it never sees (the RAU->RCU command is RCU's). Predicate state travels once per migration, not beside every GPR row (arch open A-1). The PC groups are not here: FET owns them, and they travel on ccv_fet_pca_mig.

channels.name: ccv_pca_rcu_mig
channels.doc: Architectural state back in on restore, one 1024-bit row per message in the same row numbering as ccv_rcu_pca_mig (0 to 15 GPRs, 16 and up predicate state), addressed by warp_id and mig_row so RCU writes it without state. RCU consumes a row only once it holds the warp's map (ccv_ooe_rcu_map, which it pairs with ccv_rau_rcu_mig in either order, A-45) and writes the row as it consumes it, so a row's credit coming back means the row is written (TI-13). The PC groups and their lane masks return to FET on ccv_pca_fet_mig.

channels.name: ccv_fet_pca_mig
channels.doc: A demoted warp's divergence state, out to the parked array: each lane's PC within the warp's window (CCV_W_LANE_PC bits, lane 0 at the LSBs), the PC bits above the window that every lane shares, the fairness rule's lane pointer and pick counter (DA's response IS-17), and live_mask, the lanes that have not exited (AR's response TI-27 (b)). FET's live mask is speculative: fetching an exit clears its group's lanes, every lane a rewind beat names is live again, and a mispredict restores the mask from the branch's checkpoint. After the demotion's beats it is exact, so FET sends it then. The fairness state is not the boundary's, which FET cannot know (TI-27 (c)): FET keeps its pointer, moved on to the next live lane if it names none, and sets the counter to CCV_FAIR_N, so lane r's group takes the first pick after the restore. Groups are the lanes with equal PCs; nothing else of FET's needs to move. FET owns the PCs, so they migrate from FET directly, not through RCU, which would cross two blocks and hold state it has no other reason to touch. FET sends it once OOE's rewind beats have set the PCs to the retirement boundary (TI-24 (3)). RAU sequences this and the RCU to PCA transfer; PCA acks both halves at once on ccv_pca_rau_mig_done. Checkpoints never migrate: demotion squashes to the retirement boundary, so a demoted warp has no unresolved branch. Its trace identity, trace-only like every channel's, is the instruction the warp resumes at, its retirement boundary (class instr, not none like the other migration channels): a trace-driven FET resumes there in the oracle's order, and the trace shows where each restored warp picked up (TI).

channels.name: ccv_pca_fet_mig
channels.doc: A restored warp's divergence state back to FET, in ccv_fet_pca_mig's layout: per-lane PCs, the shared upper bits, the fairness pointer and counter, and the live lanes. FET resumes fetch from them. Its trace identity, trace-only like every channel's, is the instruction the warp resumes at, its retirement boundary (class instr, not none like the other migration channels): a trace-driven FET resumes there in the oracle's order, and the trace shows where each restored warp picked up (TI).

channels.name: ccv_rau_fet_mig
channels.doc: The migration command to FET, the same command ccv_rau_rcu_mig gives RCU: which warp, which direction. On demotion FET sends the warp's PC groups on ccv_fet_pca_mig. RAU sequences both halves of a migration, so both halves need the command. tier1_id is the warp's tier-1 slot (A-65): on a restore, the slot RAU is placing it in, which FET needs before PCA's PC groups arrive; on a demotion, the slot being vacated.

channels.name: ccv_pca_rau_mig_done
channels.doc: A migration has landed, either way. direction 0: a demotion, PCA holds every row from RCU and the PC groups from FET for warp_id, and RAU may reallocate the warp's slot. direction 1: a restore, every row PCA sent to RCU on ccv_pca_rcu_mig has had its credit back, so RCU has written it, and PCA has sent the PC groups to FET; RAU may activate the warp. PCA sends it only once the last row's credit is back: a row sent but still in RCU's receiver, waiting for the warp's map, is not written, and a warp activated on it could read the row before it lands. Done means written (TI-13). One ack from the block that sees both halves, rather than one from each sender (arch open A-3; the restore COMMAND is Q-39).

channels.name: ccv_rau_pca_mig
channels.doc: The migration command to PCA (AR's response TI-24 (1); repo Q-39), the third beside ccv_rau_rcu_mig and ccv_rau_fet_mig: which warp, which direction, and its place in the parked array. RAU allocates the place from a free list of CCV_PARKED_WARPS on a demotion and frees it once the warp is restored, so PCA stores by place and holds no table. direction 0: PCA files the rows from RCU and the PCs from FET at pca_place, and acks on ccv_pca_rau_mig_done once it holds both. direction 1: PCA sends the warp's rows on ccv_pca_rcu_mig and its PCs on ccv_pca_fet_mig, then acks direction 1 once every row's credit is back (done means written, TI-13). It replaces bank_select on the other two commands, which reached only RCU and FET, neither of which stores anything.

channels.name: ccv_miu_rau_ready
channels.doc: A demoted warp is ready to restore (AR's response TI-21, rev 107; OA's rev 160): MIU sends its warp_id when the warp's count of orphaned loads, the requests a bulk discard abandoned at DCU, returns to zero. Then every line the warp asked for has landed in DCU, so its replayed loads hit after the restore; a restore before then would replay into the same miss and hold the slot again. Only MIU sees the orphan drop, so MIU counts, one counter per warp context (CCV_WARP_CONTEXTS, each up to 2^CCV_P_W_REQ_MIU_DCU). A kill clears a warp's count with no report. RAU restores a parked warp only once it is ready. RAU already sends to MIU (ccv_rau_miu_cta), so the blocks touch.

channels.name: ccv_rau_miu_cta
channels.doc: Per-CTA scratchpad bounds and the launch block address, so MIU can check F-SHARED and service launch-block reads. The CTA's .shared region is SPM bytes spm_base to spm_limit, both included, so a region may end at SPM's last byte within CCV_W_SPM_ADDR. A .shared address is the CTA-relative offset, modulo 2^32 (CP-33). MIU raises F-SHARED, cause 7, on any active lane whose bytes do not all lie within offset 0 to spm_limit - spm_base. It ranks after F-ADDR, which no .shared access can raise, and before F-RO, which only .global can raise (section 12.5). SPM's byte address is spm_base plus the offset (TI's rev 230). F-RO (O-51, O-61; AR's responses TI-26, revs 124-126): const_base and const_limit are the module's .const range, flat addresses (O-54), half-open [const_base, const_limit); equal, the range is empty. They come from the grid's descriptor (Q-50), set by its module, so they are per CTA. MIU raises F-RO, cause 8, on any lane in active_mask of a store or atomic any byte of which lies in that range or in the launch window, window 2 (address bits [47:16] equal to 2; the whole window is read-only, ISA section 5.2), compared on the effective address before MIU maps it. Loads are unaffected. F-RO is last among the execute causes (section 12.5). The instruction then has no effect on any lane: a store puts nothing committable in the store buffer, and an atomic sends no exclusive request. The completion's lane_mask is the faulting lanes, and its address the lowest such lane's.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_syu_bar
channels.doc: Barrier reports at retire (TI-40: AR's revs 161-164, OA's revs 200-204, DA 2026-10-23). OOE sends one for every retired bar.arrive, bar.wait and bar.wait.phase, and for every retired exit, partial or final; nothing leaves OOE before it retires, so no report is recalled. bar_kind: 0 arrive, 1 wait, 2 wait.phase, 3 exit. issue_mask is the uop's issue group; guard_mask its guard's lanes (all ones for an unguarded uop): an arrive's arriving lanes are issue_mask & guard_mask, an exit's exiting lanes issue_mask. A wait's lanes ask SYU for its answer; wait.phase's phase_mask is each lane's expected phase, its predicate source read at issue (O-27). held (DA's PF-44 variant, AR's rev 163/164): the wait carried FET's all_waiting mark, so its warp is converged and OOE holds rename behind it; SYU answers a held wait on ccv_syu_ooe_rel and every other wait per lane on ccv_syu_fet_rel. barrier_id is don't-care on an exit. SYU keeps the arrived lanes per (warp context, barrier id) and the live lanes per context, from the launch and the exits (SYU spec rev 7). A warp may be demoted while waiting, so the table tracks non-resident warps.

channels.name: ccv_syu_ooe_rel
channels.doc: SYU's answer to a held wait (TI-40, DA's PF-44 variant): the converged warp's barrier has completed, and OOE lifts the rename hold behind its retired wait. One answer per held wait, after it retires; a wait FET parked (not held) is answered on ccv_syu_fet_rel instead, never here, so no answer reaches a later wait (AR's rev 164). If it lands while OOE holds nothing for the warp (a squash or a demotion took the wait), OOE drops it. It is in a demotion's drain.
channels.id_classes_why: A release wakes a SET of waiting warps and has no single owning transaction. The link back to each bar.sync is already in the trace -- the arrives on the same barrier_id since its previous release -- so no set-valued id is needed; an explicit link, if wanted, is a trace event.

channels.name: ccv_syu_fet_rel
channels.doc: SYU's answer to a retired wait FET parked (TI-40, AR's rev 161): lane_mask is the lanes released, those of the wait whose barrier has completed, or was already met when the wait retired (a guard false, its own arrival complete, the phase reached). FET clears their waiting bits in the current state and every live checkpoint of the warp's slot, so a later mispredict cannot park them again. Exactly one answer per lane of each retired wait, so no answer reaches a later wait. For a context that is not resident SYU sends ccv_syu_rau_ready instead. In a demotion's drain, so an answer in flight lands before FET migrates.

channels.name: ccv_syu_rau_ready
channels.doc: A parked warp's barrier answer (TI-40, AR's rev 161): SYU answers a wait of a context that is not resident by telling RAU the warp is ready, and answers a demote op at once with it when the context has no waiting lanes. RAU restores it; FET rewound its waiting lanes to their waits at the demotion, so they fetch the wait again and ask again, which is exact since a wait has no side effect.

channels.name: ccv_rau_syu_alloc
channels.doc: Barrier entries and residency at SYU (TI-40, AR's revs 159 and 161). syu_alloc_op: 0 free (the CTA's last warp gone: its entries and slot), 1 allocate (a CTA admitted whole: barrier_base and barrier_count, the launch's, 0 to 16; warp_mask the CTA's warp contexts; warp_id its last warp and last_lanes that warp's live lanes less one, every other warp's 32, so SYU's live lanes start from the launch), 2 demote (warp_id leaves residency: SYU answers its waits on ccv_syu_rau_ready, at once if it has no waiting lanes), 3 restore (warp_id is resident again). Exits clear live lanes through OOE's exit reports on ccv_ooe_syu_bar, the final exit's included, so there is no exit op.

channels.name: ccv_ooe_cru_fault
channels.doc: The first fault taken by a context, written once and never overwritten.

channels.name: ccv_cru_rau_cfg
channels.doc: Host-programmed policy (demotion threshold, progress threshold, launch enable) and the host's kill request with a grid selector. Both kill sources -- a fault from OOE, a request from the host -- land at RAU, the single issuer.

channels.name: ccv_ext_exb_in
channels.doc: TileLink TL-C, inbound: channels B (probe) and D (grant). Declared now rather than with a second core, because it is the only way the testbench memory can INITIATE a probe -- and so the only way to exercise the DCU probe port, probe as a wake source, and a probe arriving at a sleeping block before there is a second core to debug them with. A probe's line address and type ride in tl_in's TL-B fields; EXB turns them into ccv_exb_mlc_rsp's phys_addr and probe_type.

channels.name: ccv_dcu_miu_fill_ntc
channels.doc: A refill notice (OA-23; AR's response TI-23): DCU promises that the refill answering req_id leaves on the same slot of ccv_dcu_miu_rsp with its valid exactly CCV_LAT_FILL_NOTICE cycles after this notice's payload lands. DCU keeps the promise by reserving that slot and its credit, and a probe never cancels a promised response (DCU spec, Internals). Optional: a refill without a notice is legal and only wakes its dependants late. MIU uses it to send OOE's completion hint in time (ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl_hint). A channel of its own rather than a second valid in the response's slot: a notice is a message with its own valid, and as a channel its payload register is enabled by its own valid flop (CG-5), with no lead slice.

slot_attrs_why.ordering: each notice names its refill by req_id, and its slot is its refill's
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: the promise counts cycles from the notice's landing, which means something only if MIU takes every notice the cycle it lands

channels.notice_of_why: OA-23: MIU must know a refill's arrival CCV_LAT_CMPL_HINT + CCV_LAT_MIU_FILL cycles ahead to hint OOE's completion 2 cycles ahead of its valid; AR's response TI-23 chose a notice channel over a second valid in the slot

channels.name: ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl_hint
channels.doc: A completion hint (OA-23; AR's response TI-23): MIU promises that the completion of rob_tag, waking RS entry rs_idx, leaves on the same slot of ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl with its valid exactly CCV_LAT_CMPL_HINT cycles after this hint's payload lands, so OOE's wake lines can rise two cycles ahead of the completion as its scheduler loop needs (OI-45). MIU keeps it by reserving the completion's slot and credit, and those of the load's data on ccv_miu_rcu_data (MIU spec, Mechanisms). Optional: a completion without a hint wakes a cycle late. rob_tag, not a generation bit, tells a stale hint: OOE acts only if that ROB slot is not squashed-pending (AR's rev 94, OA's rev 141).

slot_attrs_why.ordering: each hint names its completion by rob_tag, and its slot is its completion's
slot_attrs_why.fixed_latency: the promise counts cycles from the hint's landing, which means something only if OOE takes every hint the cycle it lands

channels.notice_of_why: OA-23: OOE's wake for a miss completion must rise two cycles before it, which the completion's own valid, one cycle ahead of its payload, cannot give

_field_ownership_comment: OWNERSHIP (Q-34): a field that crosses hops is owned by this schema, not
by the sessions that consume it. Its width and encoding are the ones here,
on every channel that carries it. A block may narrow a field locally only
if its encoding is a strict projection of the shared one -- low bits of
the same code, never a re-encoding. opcode stays at DEC's width on all
three hops until the ISA opcode census says otherwise; asid (8) and size
(a 3-bit code) already have one width everywhere.
per_hop_fields are the exception, and are not cross-hop at all: req_id
names one hop's outstanding request, sized by that hop's window, so each
hop has its own. Only these may carry a per-channel width override;
tools/gen-interfaces.py refuses an override of any other field.
_field_widths_comment: Payload field -> width, as a SystemVerilog expression over ccv_params_pkg
and ccv_prov_pkg. A field absent from this map has no decided width, so
its channel generates a field LIST rather than a packed struct, and
Inventing the missing ones here would put a number nobody decided into a
generated typedef, and generated numbers get believed. They are enumerated
instead, so the ask to each per-block session is a specific short list.
_open_questions_comment: Questions the payload pass raised that are NOT width questions, and that
no width can close. Each blocks something specific; the `blocks` field
says what, so it is obvious when one has become urgent. Each carries its
id in docs/open-items.md, where it is numbered once and never reused;
tools/check-docs.sh requires the two to agree.

rcu_miu_width.question: ccv_rcu_miu_addr carries index_per_lane (1024) beside store_data (1024) at rate 4 -- roughly 8,400 wires from RCU into MIU, almost certainly the widest interface in the design. It argues for co-locating the AGUs with RCU, or moving address generation into the register read stage.
rcu_miu_width.kind: partitioning question that a width exposed
rcu_miu_width.blocks: Nothing today -- the skeleton does not care how wide a bus is. Settle before floorplan rather than after, since the answer may move a block boundary and block boundaries are swap boundaries.

_rate_comment: `rate` is TRANSFERS per cycle at peak -- messages, not bits. The source
spec gives the two migration channels as '1024b', a bandwidth: one
1024-bit GPR row per cycle, i.e. rate 1, with the row carried in the
payload's gpr_row field. The first encoding dropped the 'b' and stored
rate 1024, which the skeleton would have built as 1024 parallel slots.
_slot_attrs_comment: 2026-09-25). A rate>1 channel is `rate` independent credited slots -- the
permissive superset -- tightened per channel as block sessions decide.
Only DECIDED values are written on a channel, each with a reason; the
generators apply the permissive default otherwise and report which is
which, so a default is never mistaken for a decision.
`lockstep` is an INSTANCE-level attribute: it describes the copies of a
channel across a multi-instance endpoint, not the slots within one copy.

acceptance.doc: atomic: a group of messages moves together -- valids and credits both all-or-none across the slots, since a message is its valid AND its payload despite the one-cycle stagger. Checked by ccv_common_chk_atomic; lets RTL collapse to one counter.

slot_binding.doc: bound: slot index carries meaning, so slots are NOT interchangeable. `binding_group` gives the slots per group (default 1: every slot its own stream). The one attribute that cannot be recovered later.

binding_group.doc: Slots per binding group; must divide the rate. fet->dec is four warp streams of two, so 2.

ordering.doc: An ordering KEY, not a boolean. none: no order across slots. slot_group: one program order within each binding group. A payload field name (e.g. warp_id): ordered among messages with the same value of that field, and free between values -- six uops from up to four warps have no total order, only a per-warp one.

lockstep.applies: a channel replicated across a multi-instance endpoint
lockstep.doc: All instances advance together: slot k's valid and credit are the same on every instance each cycle, and -- with the trace sideband -- carry the same instruction id. Checked by ccv_common_chk_lockstep. Without it, 32 lanes with per-lane flow control is not a SIMD machine.

fixed_latency.doc: true: the receiver never asserts stall and returns a credit for every message the cycle it lands, so a message's arrival time is fixed by the sender's schedule. The OOE fixed-latency contract rests on it (A-47): OOE schedules wakeup from contracted latencies with no grant, late or cancel signal. Checked by ccv_common_chk_credit's FIXED_LAT properties.

_id_classes_comment: Which trace-identity classes a channel's messages may carry (interface
decisions, 2026-09-24): instr -- work traceable to a fetched instruction;
txn -- a transaction with no single owning instruction, or one of one
instruction's many; none -- probes, launches, migration, CSR access.
A SET, because some channels carry more than one kind: EXB->MLC and the
inbound external port carry fills (txn) and probes (none). The skeleton
checks every message against its channel's set. The per-channel
assignment is the skeleton's proposal against those definitions, not yet
a block session's decision -- see docs/skeleton.md.
